comments.author: RaiRaiTheRaichu Staff
comments.body_html:
A brief notice, just to clarify for anyone who may intend to create replacement bundles and upload them as mods:

As per the File Submission Guidelines, bundles that are edited and are intended to replace the original game assets are not allowed to be uploaded as a mod. Loading the bundles via a server-side mod is, of course, completely fine - replacing original ones are not.

Under section for “Inappropriate Content”:

Files may not replace existing EFT or SPT data. File overwriting or other forms of destructive edits are forbidden. All files must edit values at launch using the mod loader.

comments.author: DarkonX
comments.body_html:
Hello everyone, it took me a while to figure this out, but my solution is simple. When you use asset editor and export a texture make sure you export the texture as TGA. Do not and I repeat do NOT use PNG. PNG files will ‘merge’ the visual texture with the alpha channel into 1 single file. Where as TGA will keep the visual texture and alpha channel as separate files.

Once you export the TGA texture and use your preferred editor (I use Photoshop) you should be able to see the Alpha texture as a separate file. You can edit the visual texture as you wish and you can also edit the alpha texture as you wish separately. Once you’re done you have to save your edited texture as TGA (once again do NOT use PNG). I also recommend keeping the dimensions of the textures all the same.

When back on asset editor you import your new TGA file and inject it. Once you inject it the tool will say something like “The original texture has transparency. Apply this transparency to the new image?” You have to select ‘no’. I you select ‘yes’ I think Asset Editor will use the original alpha channel on the original unedited texture; whereas if you select ‘no’ it will use the alpha channel in your edited file.

I’ve had success working like this, but let me know what ya’ll think.
